A locally-led NGO · Kiribati

Cultivating a Resilient Kiribati

For generations, the people of Kiribati have cultivated the bwabwai (giant taro). Growing this vital crop in harsh atoll soils has always required specialized knowledge, careful planning, and constant adaptation to the environment. Today, our people face a similar challenge. The environment around us is changing, and our communities need new tools, new knowledge, and careful planning to thrive. Empower Kiribati exists to help our people cultivate a strong, resilient future in a rapidly shifting world.

For generations, our people have grown the bwabwai in harsh atoll soils — work that has always demanded knowledge, planning, and constant adaptation. Today our communities face the same test, and need new tools to meet it.

The Changing Soil

The Threats to Our Roots

Just as rising tides threaten the roots of the bwabwai, modern challenges are threatening the roots of our livelihoods, our culture, and our well-being. Today, our communities are facing unprecedented pressures:

01
Climate Change Washing away shorelines and contaminating the freshwater and soil we depend on for survival.

Create Conditions for Innovation

When the environment shifts, we help communities test, learn, and adapt new ways of growing food, preserving culture, and building climate resilience so solutions are owned locally.

02
Unemployment Leaving our youth with few pathways to earn a living, straining households and forcing people into vulnerable informal work.

Enable Livelihoods & Enterprise

When traditional jobs are scarce, we teach practical money management and help entrepreneurs build viable businesses, creating new economic opportunities that do not rely on a limited job market.

03
Digital Isolation Creating a divide, locking people out of the modern tools needed to connect, learn, and earn safely.

Enable Digital Participation

When the world moves online, we build the digital literacy and cyber-safety skills our people need to navigate the internet confidently, ensuring no one is left behind.

04
Fragile Leadership Progress often relies on too few people, making it difficult for communities to sustain long-term change.

Empower Leaders & Communities

When progress is fragile, we develop local stewards and build strong organizational frameworks so that communities can lead their own changes long after external funding ends.

The Adaptation

How We Adapt: Our Roots of Empowerment

Like the successful growth of the bwabwai, our ability to survive these challenges requires a healthy root system and the ability to adapt. Empower Kiribati does not just offer temporary relief; we provide the specialized knowledge and care needed to address these threats permanently.

Creating Conditions for Innovation

Innovation in Kiribati isn’t only about new technology — it’s about creating the conditions where communities, local organizations, and young people can test ideas, learn quickly, and improve what already works. Across dispersed islands, solutions must be practical, low-cost, and adaptable to different atoll realities. We help turn local insights into workable pilots that can grow into sustainable programs. We focus on the systems that make innovation possible: access to information, basic tools and infrastructure, skills training, and spaces where people can collaborate. That includes supporting community-led problem solving, strengthening local institutions to plan and deliver projects, and using evidence to guide decisions — not assumptions. By building pathways from small experiments to wider adoption, we help communities move from “trying something once” to developing resilient, repeatable approaches. Over time, this creates a culture of learning and improvement that strengthens climate resilience, livelihoods, and services — even when resources are limited.

Enabling Digital Participation

As services, education, and economic opportunities increasingly move online, digital inclusion becomes a matter of fairness and resilience. We work to ensure I-Kiribati communities — including women, youth, and outer island residents — can participate safely and confidently in the digital world, not be left behind by connectivity gaps or low digital literacy. Our work supports practical access and capability: foundational digital skills, trusted information, and tools that help people use digital services for real needs — applying for opportunities, accessing learning, managing finances, and staying connected to networks and support. We also prioritize digital trust and safety. Communities need to understand online risks, protect personal information, and navigate misinformation. By strengthening digital confidence and responsibility, we help people use technology as an enabler of opportunity — expanding education, improving livelihoods, and supporting stronger community connections across every atoll.

Building Partnership for Impact

No single organization can meet the scale of challenges facing Kiribati alone — especially across a nation of scattered atolls where resources, services, and opportunities are unevenly distributed. We build partnerships that respect local leadership and bring together government, community groups, churches, schools, diaspora networks, and the private sector so that solutions are coordinated, culturally grounded, and practical to deliver. Our approach is to connect strengths: local knowledge and trusted relationships, technical expertise, funding, and delivery capacity. By aligning partners around shared goals and clear roles, we reduce duplication and ensure projects are designed with communities — not simply delivered to them. Strong partnerships also help ideas move from pilot to long-term programs, with the right support systems in place for maintenance, training, and continued learning. Partnerships are also how we grow impact beyond a single project. When we collaborate openly, share evidence, and invest in long-term relationships, we can unlock better services, stronger local organizations, and more resilient livelihoods — while ensuring benefits reach women, youth, and outer island communities.

Empowering Leaders & Communities

We believe lasting change in Kiribati must be led locally — by people who understand the rhythms of island life, the realities of outer atolls, and the strengths already present in community networks. When leadership is rooted in culture and community priorities, solutions are more relevant, more trusted, and far more likely to endure beyond a single project or funding cycle. That’s why we invest in building capability and leadership pathways: training, mentorship, and practical opportunities that help emerging leaders gain confidence, skills, and support. By strengthening local organizations, youth and women’s leadership, and community decision-making, we help communities move from being recipients of support to being designers and drivers of their own development. Empowered communities are also better prepared to navigate climate pressures, economic uncertainty, and the rapid shift to digital services. When people have the knowledge, tools, and voice to advocate for themselves, they can protect what matters, take informed risks, and build inclusive opportunities for the next generation — on their own terms.
